description:
Detector findings in `crystal_rules.ml` use four different message styles. Mixed styles make it hard for downstream consumers (formatter, IDE integration) to parse and hurt the user experience.

**Style 1 — colon-separated with explanation:**
- `"puts used for debugging"` (deprecated-syntax)
- `"Pointer.malloc is unsafe — use Slice or Array for safe memory management"`
- `"Empty rescue block — errors are silently swallowed. Log or handle the exception."`

**Style 2 — em-dash, "consider X":**
- `"String.join" — Array.join(separator) — join is on Array, not String`
- `"Manual while loop with counter — consider using .each, .map, or .each_with_index"`
- `"Function 'foo' has 8 parameters (max 6) — group into a configuration record"`

**Style 3 — parens with current value:**
- `"Function 'foo' has %d AST nodes (max %d) — consider breaking into smaller functions"`
- `"Function 'foo' has %d boolean operators (max %d) — extract into named predicates"`
- `"Regex %s duplicated in functions: %s — extract to a constant"`

**Style 4 — line-number inline:**
- `"Unreachable code after raise/error on line %d"`
- `"Unreachable code after terminal statement on line %d"`

**Proposed standard format:**

```
<rule subject>: <observation> — <actionable suggestion>
```

Examples:
- `puts: debug print used in production — replace with structured logging or remove`
- `Pointer.malloc: unsafe raw memory allocation — use Slice or Array for safe memory management`
- `Function 'foo' (8 parameters): exceeds 6-parameter guideline — group related parameters into a configuration record`
- `Regex '/foo/': duplicated across functions bar, baz — extract to a named constant`

**Implementation:** introduce a `finding` constructor in `crystal_rules_helpers.ml`:

```ocaml
val mk_finding : rule_id:string -> severity:Types.severity -> line:int -> subject:string -> observation:string -> suggestion:string -> Types.finding
```

and a formatter helper that ensures every message follows the standard. Detectors stop calling `Printf.sprintf "..."` and instead call the helper. This also lets us keep the `rule_id` close to its message and stop threading it through `all ()`.

**Risk:** This WILL change message text. Downstream tools that grep message text will break. Need to grep `Catseye` consumers for any string-matching tests:
```
grep -rn 'Pointer.malloc' /workspaces/catseye/src /workspaces/catseye/test
grep -rn 'manual loop' /workspaces/catseye/src /workspaces/catseye/test
```
(Confirm none exist before landing.)

Blocks: catseye-ozj (refactor epic)
Depends on: catseye-4o6 (split into submodules)

comments.text: Deferred — message format standardization needs design input. The current 4 styles in crystal_rules.ml are documented in the original ticket description. The 'right' format depends on user preference (single-line vs multi-line, severity emoji vs severity word, em-dash vs colon, etc.). A follow-up ticket should land the format choice as a separate decision before doing the 30+ text changes.

title: REFACTOR: standardize error message format and emitter helper
